newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Consortium bids for Orrefors Kosta Boda.
newsitem.headline: Consortium bids for Orrefors Kosta Boda.

text.p: A consortium of Swedish investment group Proventus AB, Denmark's Royal Copenhagen and Scandinavian Equity Partners Ltd -- a Swedish/American investment company -- on Tuesday made a takeover bid for Swedish glassmaker Orrefors Kosta Boda.
The consortium said in a statement that it was bidding 155 crowns a share and the company's main shareholder Investor AB had already agreed to sell its 23.1 percent stake.
The move ended weeks of speculation over the future ownership of the quality glassmaker as both Proventus and Royal Copenhagen had raised their stakes this month.
The consortium said it already had control of 73.9 percent of capital and votes in Orrefors Kosta Boda.
Royal Copenhagen, which is 82 percent owned by Danish brewer Carlsberg AS, raised its holding in the glass company to 17.1 percent earlier this month.
This prompted Proventus, fearing a Danish takeover, to lift its stake to 21.1 percent with an option to take a further 9.1 percent stake.
Proventus also bid 145 crowns a share to shareholders in Orrefors for shares corresponding to 20 percent of the capital in the company.
Trading in Orrefors was suspended on Friday when the three key shareholders announced they had started talks over future ownership. The last trade was at 140 crowns.
"The consortium has decided to work together to strengthen Orrefors Kosta Boda both in Sweden and internationally," the group said in a statement.
"The aim is furthermore to develop Orrefors Kosta Boda's product range and strengthen this brand."
The consortium said this takeover offer expanded on a marketing cooperation agreement agreed between Orrefors Kosta Boda and Royal Copenhagen in July this year.

The consortium wil be owned 42.5 percent by Proventus, which is the investment vehicle of Swedish financier Robert Weil, 42.5 percent by Scandinavian Equity Partners Ltd and 15 percent percent by Royal Copenhagen.
Scandinavian Equity Partners was set up at the end of 1994 by Investor, S-E-Banken and U.S. company AEA Investors Inc and specialises in management buy-outs.
